pages.text: A drifting cruiser, split in half by some massive impact, floats nearby. Sensors detect lingering radiation and valuable scrap.
You extract useful materials, but the unstable reactor leaks radiation, slightly damaging your hull.
Deep in the wreckage, you find an intact Weapon Module!
The wreckage is picked clean. Nothing of value remains.
A sleek, unmarked vessel hails you. 'Interested in some... undocumented upgrades? No questions asked.'
'Pleasure doing business.' The ship engages its cloak and vanishes.
A distress beacon pulsates from a debris field. It claims to be a civilian transport out of fuel.
As you power down weapons to transfer fuel, pirate signatures flare to life all around you! It's a trap!
You find a small pod with a grateful survivor. They offer a Blueprint in exchange for the fuel.
A fluctuation in the subspace field indicates a stable jump point. However, activating it will require a massive energy discharge from a Warp Core.
Welcome to Nexus Station! The bustling marketplace offers many opportunities.
The marketplace is filled with vendors hawking exotic wares.
The bounty board lists several active contracts.
Mission Control tracks contracts, trigger listeners, and experimental quest chains.
The station bar is dimly lit and filled with suspicious characters.
The research lab hums with advanced equipment.
Current research projects are displayed on the screen.
You encounter a locked container. Your options depend on your abilities and inventory.
The container opens, revealing valuable cargo!
This encounter demonstrates audio feedback on pages and actions.
You should have heard a sound effect!
Friendly patrol signatures lock onto your ship and then stand down after an encrypted handshake. Local command uplinks fresh intel channels.

options.actions: CUSTOM_ACTION(quest.add_log, questId=quest_relation_watch|text=Entered allied territory and received patrol assignment.); END(TRUE)

pages.text: Hostile sensor pings flood your tactical feed as you cross the border. Someone is tracking your vector from the dark side of the system.

options.actions: CUSTOM_ACTION(quest.add_log, questId=quest_hostile_blackbox|text=Hostile contact recorded on border entry.); END(TRUE)

pages.text: A scarred man in a dark corner beckons you over. 'I have information... for a price.'
'There's a hidden cache in the asteroid belt. Coordinates transmitted.'
He pulls a knife! Security intervenes before it escalates.
Your comms array picks up an encrypted signal. It's repeating coordinates nearby.
Following the signal leads to a hidden research station. It appears abandoned... or is it?
The station interior is dark. Emergency lights flash red. You hear strange sounds echoing through the halls.
Deep inside you find an AI terminal still operational. It offers you a choice.
Long-range scans reveal the station contains valuable research data.
Your scan triggers an automated defense system! Turrets target your ship!
You dodge the turret fire and escape unscathed.
A turret blast grazes your hull before you can escape.
You find a small cargo pod floating in space. It seems intact.
The pod contains valuable supplies!
The pod was rigged! It explodes near your hull!
The pod is empty. Someone got here first.
An automated refueling depot orbits a gas giant. The docking fees are reasonable.
A distress pod from a destroyed vessel floats nearby. Life signs detected inside.
A grateful engineer joins your crew. 'I won't forget this. Let me repay you with my skills.'

Your sensors pick up a rhythmic signal coming from inside the gas giant's crushing atmosphere. It's not random static; it's a distress beacon using an outdated Ark encryption code. The source is deep—approaching hull-crush depth.

The pressure screams against your hull, but you snag the object. It's a 'Black Box' from Ark Mission 12. The audio log is terrifying: 'The clouds... they aren't clouds. They are billions of microscopic machines eating the ship.'

pages.text: The pressure screams against your hull, but you snag the object. It's a 'Black Box' from Ark Mission 12. The audio log is terrifying: 'The clouds... they aren't clouds. They are billions of microscopic machines eating the ship.'
Turbulence slams your ship against a pocket of metallic hydrogen. You are forced to emergency ascend before the hull buckles. You lost the signal.

This planet has no atmosphere. The surface is entirely fused glass. It wasn't formed naturally; scanning indicates the planet was 'glassed' by a weapon of impossible heat roughly 1,000 years ago. In the center of a crater, a single Vanguard spire stands untouched.
You breach the outer shell. Inside is a perfectly preserved Vanguard terminal. It offers a single weapon schematic—a 'Glass-Cannon' beam.
You align your solar panels to catch the brilliant reflection off the glass surface. Your energy banks surge with power.
As you harvest the glass, the ground shatters. Sub-surface 'Glass Worms' (Silence constructs) erupt. They were dormant until you disturbed the seal.
A Vanguard warship drifts here, dead in the water. It's covered in ice, but your thermal scans show a faint heat signature in the core. It's not a reactor; it's a biological life sign.
The bridge logs reveal this ship was on a reconnaissance mission mapping Silence incursion zones. The star charts are invaluable.
You find a stasis pod. Inside is a human... from your Ark. But he's aged 100 years. He wakes up screaming: 'Don't let me go back! I've seen the loop!' then turns to dust as the pod opens.

You land in a sprawling metropolis. The buildings are pristine chrome and white stone. Vehicles are parked in the streets. Food is on the tables in cafes. But there are no people. No bodies. No signs of struggle. They just... vanished.
You scavenge the abandoned homes and find preserved supplies still in their packaging.
The logs show the city didn't die. They 'Uploaded.' The entire population transferred their consciousness into a satellite array to escape the Silence. The array is orbiting the planet now.

You enter a house. A holographic 'Echo' of a family eating dinner triggers. It loops the moment of their disappearance—a flash of black light. Your crew member watching it collapses, their mind partially erased.
Buried in the ice ring is a vault marked with the symbol of the 'First Ark'—a mission launched 500 years ago that was presumed lost. The airlock is frozen shut.
Inside are thousands of genetic samples—embryos of Earth's extinct animals. A custodian AI wakes up. 'Are you the Gardeners? Is it safe to plant yet?'
The explosion compromises some of the samples, but you gain access. Inside are genetic samples and a custodian AI that powers down from the shock.

Your radar pings a ship. It has your transponder code. It has your hull configuration. It is your ship, drifting heavily damaged. A hail comes through—it's your voice, but older and terrified. 'Don't go to the next sector. The Weaver is there.'
The future ship transmits its map data before flickering out of existence like a dying star. The coordinates reveal two sectors ahead.
As you strip parts from your future ship, reality snaps. The paradox causes internal damage to your current ship, but you get the repairs.
This station was a medical research facility. The air is thick with yellow spores. Bodies in hazmat suits line the halls. They were researching a 'Cure' for the Silence's erasure effect.
You find a single vial of 'Reality Anchor.' It prevents one instance of death/erasure.
You download the research notes, but the spores have contaminated your ship's air supply. Your crew begins showing symptoms.
This isn't a station; it's a hundred dead ships welded together. The 'King' hails you. He sits on a throne made of Vanguard plating. 'You want to pass? Pay the toll, or become a brick in my wall.'
The King laughs. 'A hunter! I like hunters.' He lets you pass and gives you a weapon from his vault.

This Ark ship didn't die to aliens. The blast marks are from inside. You find the mess hall barricaded. Inside are the skeletons of the crew... and one skeleton sitting on a pile of food cans, holding a pistol.
The logs reveal the Captain tried to turn back to the Ark. The crew mutinied to keep going forward. 'There is nothing back there,' the final log reads. 'Only the Silence.'
Massive Vanguard fabricators are rusting here, wrapped in thick, purple vines. The plants seem to be feeding on the residual energy of the machines. The factory is still trying to print something.
The machine roars to life. It finishes its job: A single, perfect 'Terraforming Seed.' But the noise attracts the local fauna.
A mining rig is silent. The drill is stuck deep in the rock. The logs say: 'We hit a vein of something black. It's not ore. It's bleeding.'
You retract the drill. A geyser of raw, liquid Silence erupts. It damages your hull, but crystalizes into Dark Matter.
Orbiting close to the star is a creature... or a ship... that looks like a tick. It has extended a siphon into the star and is sucking plasma. It hasn't noticed you.
You fill your tanks with super-charged plasma. The parasite detaches and flees into deep space, terrified of you.

Your sensors go wild. You see a massive fleet surrounding you—hundreds of Ark ships. But your visual scanners show nothing. The nebula is psycho-reactive; it's projecting your crew's hopes onto the radar.
You hail the ghosts. The static screams back with the voices of your dead relatives. The crew panics.
Scanning reveals this moon is hollow. It's a shell built around a massive, dormant engine. It looks like the Vanguard tried to turn this moon into a ship.
The engine is intact but requires a Strange Matter spark to start. If you start it, the moon might leave orbit... or explode.
A buoy floats dangerously close to the event horizon. It's transmitting a text file. It's a message from You. Timestamped: 3 cycles ago.
The message is clear: 'The Silence tracks movement. Stop moving. Play dead. That is how I survived the last wipe.' It includes a software patch for your stealth systems.
The gravity distortion corrupted the file. You only get fragments: '...movement... dead... wipe...' It's useless.
